name: Barack Obama
role: Illinois state senator (1997–2004), U.S. senator (2005–2008), and 44th president (2009–2017). The board is his public stances, not every vote.

portrait.author: Pete Souza / Official White House Photo

name: Same-sex marriage
role: Supported it on a 1996 questionnaire, then civil unions without the word marriage, then became the first sitting president to back legalization in 2012.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

name: Individual mandate
role: Attacked Hillary Clinton’s 2008 requirement that people buy insurance, then put a mandate at the center of the Affordable Care Act.

name: NSA surveillance
role: Criticized Bush-era warrantless wiretapping, voted to legalize the architecture in 2008, then defended and later narrowed the programs as president.

name: Cuba opening
role: Kept the embargo while easing family travel, then restored diplomatic relations in 2014 and visited Havana in 2016.

name: DACA
role: Backed the DREAM Act in Congress, said a president could not defer deportations by fiat, then created Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals in 2012.

name: Medical marijuana
role: Pledged to stop DEA raids on state-legal dispensaries, then outpaced Bush-era raids, then told prosecutors to stand down in Cole-memo states.

name: Afghanistan surge
role: Called Afghanistan the necessary war and sent 30,000 more troops in 2009, then began a drawdown that still left thousands in place.

links.label: Foreign policy of the Obama administration

name: Iraq War
role: Opposed the 2003 invasion in a 2002 Chicago speech, ran in 2008 on a responsible end, and withdrew combat forces in 2011.

name: Affordable Care Act
role: Signature first-term law: exchanges, a Medicaid expansion, and subsidies. Coverage rose; the uninsured rate fell from about 16% to 9%.

name: Public option
role: Wanted a government insurance plan on the exchanges, then allowed the Senate to drop it so the rest of the health law could pass.

name: DADT repeal
role: Opposed the military ban on openly gay service members and signed the Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell Repeal Act in 2010.

links.label: Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act of 2010

name: Closing Guantanamo
role: Ordered the prison closed within a year of taking office. Transfers cut the population sharply; 41 men were still there when he left.

name: Iran nuclear deal
role: Pushed diplomacy over isolation, then the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action limiting Iran’s nuclear program for sanctions relief.

name: Keystone XL
role: Sat on the border-crossing permit through a long environmental review, then rejected the tar-sands pipeline in 2015.

name: Climate action
role: Wanted cap-and-trade, put clean-energy money in the stimulus, then used EPA rules and the Paris Agreement after Congress stalled.

links.label: Energy policy of the Obama administration

name: Recovery Act
role: An $800 billion blend of spending and tax cuts signed in the trough of the Great Recession, including infrastructure and clean energy.

links.label: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009

name: Dodd-Frank
role: 2010 financial rewrite: more bank oversight, a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and no full Glass–Steagall revival.

name: Assault weapons ban
role: Favored renewing the federal assault-weapons ban and tighter gun-show rules; a 1996 questionnaire also recorded a handgun ban he later denied.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

name: Death penalty
role: Kept capital punishment for the most heinous crimes while backing interrogation reforms in Illinois. No federal executions were carried out on his watch.

links.label: Social policy of the Obama administration

name: Trans-Pacific Partnership
role: Negotiated and signed the 12-nation trade pact as a Pacific pivot. Congress never ratified it.

name: Minimum wage
role: Asked Congress for a federal floor that moved from $9 toward $10.10 and later $12. The Republican Congress blocked it; many states still raised theirs.

links.label: Economic policy of the Obama administration

name: Stem-cell research
role: Co-sponsored bills to ease Bush limits, then revoked those limits by executive order in 2009.

name: Auto rescue
role: Continued and expanded the Bush-era rescue of GM and Chrysler, forcing bankruptcies and new labor terms rather than liquidation.

name: Drone strikes
role: Made armed drones a central counterterror tool, including the 2011 strike that killed Anwar al-Awlaki, a U.S. citizen, in Yemen.
